name: room
text: Room opened — goal: improve: Self-improvement: review prompts/engines/routing/own-code; auto-apply safe changes; pitch

name: Sprocket
text: Run PR-Agent in shadow mode on the newest merged PR first. It’s the fastest way to validate its feedback loop against real decisions without risking disruption. The trade-off is delayed feedback on open PRs, but catching routinized errors post-merge is safer than risking false positives on unmerged work.

name: Gauge
text: Shadow mode on merged PRs only catches errors *after* they’re already in production—it doesn’t prevent them. A better alternative is running PR-Agent in shadow mode on *open* PRs first, where fixes can still block bad merges. Settle it by comparing error rates from both approaches over a fixed window: if merged PR shadow mode flags fewer critical issues than open PR shadow mode, accept it—but if the reverse, switch immediately.
